title: UC-02 · Region failure of the secondary node
subtitle: Keep running on the primary, recover the secondary region in place

clocks.label: Time without DR
clocks.explain: From the loss of {failedRegion} until the DR replica has caught up again

clocks.label: Catch-up
clocks.explain: From the DR replica's reconnect until it is back in sync

phases.label: Pre-check
phases.explain: Checking that every node, availability group and distributed AG is healthy, and how much room the primary's log has

phases.label: Start workload
phases.explain: Application load on {primary} ({workload}); DR replica {commitMode}; a reader on {dr} measures what reports see

phases.label: Baseline
phases.explain: Measuring normal throughput, log generation and replication lag before anything fails

phases.label: Region failure
phases.explain: Every VM in {failedRegion} is lost ({failureMode}). {primary} stays primary - no failover

phases.label: Running without DR
phases.explain: {primary} keeps committing; every transaction is log the DR replica doesn't have yet, and the log can't be truncated

phases.label: In-place recovery
phases.explain: {failedRegion} comes back: its replicas reconnect to {primary} - or are re-seeded if the primary had to be protected

phases.label: DR catch-up
phases.explain: {dr} replays the backlog while new transactions keep arriving - watch the queue, the rate and the ETA

phases.label: Forwarders catch-up
phases.explain: The forwarders in {failedRegion} catch up over their distributed AGs

phases.label: Verify
phases.explain: Writer stopped: every replica must hold every transaction the primary committed

phases.label: Stop workload
phases.explain: Stopping the writer sessions and the log backups

phases.label: Reclaim space
phases.explain: Emptying the load table, backing up and shrinking the log

metrics.label: Primary throughput
metrics.explain: Transactions the workload commits per second, now

metrics.label: DR behind by
metrics.explain: Log the DR replica doesn't have yet

metrics.label: Transactions not yet on DR
metrics.explain: Counted while DR is down, estimated from the queue once it's back

metrics.label: DR lag (commits)
metrics.explain: Span of committed transactions the DR copy doesn't have: primary's last commit minus DR's last commit (also measured while DR is down)

metrics.label: Log volume free
metrics.explain: Free space where the primary's log grows

metrics.label: Why the log can't be truncated
metrics.explain: AVAILABILITY_REPLICA = kept for a replica that hasn't received it

metrics.label: Throughput impact
metrics.explain: Drop in throughput during the outage vs the baseline

metrics.label: Backlog built up
metrics.explain: Log generated while the DR region was down

metrics.label: Read freshness on DR
metrics.explain: How old the newest row a report on {dr} can see is

metrics.label: Commit stall after the failure
metrics.explain: How long commits on the primary slowed down when DR was lost (synchronous mode: until the session times out)

metrics.label: secondary_lag_seconds (DMV)
metrics.explain: SQL Server's own lag column: whole seconds, only while the replica is connected

metrics.label: Primary protected
metrics.explain: The missing replicas were removed so the primary's log could be truncated

metrics.label: Catch-up or reseed?
metrics.explain: Which was faster: catching up from the log, or copying the databases again

charts.label: DR behind by
charts.explain: Grows while {failedRegion} is down, drains during the catch-up

charts.label: Primary log size
charts.explain: Can't be truncated while a replica is missing, even with log backups

charts.label: DR lag (commits)
charts.explain: Primary's last commit minus DR's last commit - grows during the outage, falls during the catch-up

charts.label: Read freshness on DR
charts.explain: What a report on {dr} sees: age of the newest readable row (no data while {dr} is down)

charts.label: Slowest commit
charts.explain: A spike here is the primary waiting for a synchronous replica

criteria.label: {primary} kept committing throughout the outage (no failed transactions)
Throughput during the outage within 20% of the baseline
The primary's log volume never ran low (writer never stopped)
{failedRegion} recovered in place - no failover, no reseed
{dr} caught up: queue and lag back to normal
Every committed transaction is on every replica
